newsitem.title: USA: Ruling could lead to tobacco document release.
newsitem.headline: Ruling could lead to tobacco document release.

text.p: The judge hearing Florida's Medicaid lawsuit against cigarette makers ruled Thursday that the state's openness law on documents in lawsuits is constitutional, potentially paving the way for publication of thousands of secret tobacco company documents.
The ruling by Circuit Judge Harold Cohen during a pretrial hearing in the case was seen as a defeat for the tobacco companies.
It triggered the review of the documents by William Rutter, a special master appointed by Cohen who will examine the documents and judge whether they can be provided to the public.

The documents belong to the 13 tobacco companies that are defendants in Florida's lawsuit seeking to recoup $1 billion in Medicaid funds the state says it spent treating illnesses. Florida is one of 40 states that have sued the tobacoo industry to recoup Medicaid costs.

"I am directing Rutter to review the remaining documents under the Sunshine In Litigation Act and to take the next step and determine if these trade secrets contain evidence of a public hazard or not," Cohen said.
Under the act, trade secrets can be made public if they are deemed to involve something considered a hazard to the public.

The documents affected by the ruling contain information regarding cigarette additives, scientific reports governing everything from secondhand smoke to information dealing with advertising claims. They include 13 documents related to the litigation settlement by Brooke Group Ltd.'s Liggett Group, which the tobacco companies have been fighting to keep from being released.
